ip.enterAnIpv4OrIpv6Address: Enter an IPv4 or IPv6 address
ip.faq.supportedAddressesAnswer: Public IPv4 and IPv6 addresses are supported. Enter only the address, without a protocol, port or path. Private, loopback and reserved addresses cannot be used for public location lookups. Examples include 1.1.1.1 and 8.8.8.8; paste a complete address for IPv6. Addresses such as 192.168.x.x, 10.x.x.x and 127.0.0.1 are meaningful only on a local network and cannot identify a public location.
ip.faq.locationDifferences: Why do sources report different locations?
ip.faq.locationDifferencesAnswer: Sources use different collection methods and update schedules. IP geolocation estimates a network address's location, not a device's precise position. ISP names may refer to a data center or upstream network. Compare country, city, ISP and ASN instead of relying only on the city. Proxies, mobile networks, cloud servers and address reassignment can all create differences between database records and actual use.
ip.faq.networkIdentifiers: What are ASN, ISP and address type?
ip.faq.networkIdentifiersAnswer: An ASN identifies the autonomous system routing the address. ISP is the network organization recorded by the source. IPv4 and IPv6 indicate the protocol version. One ISP may have multiple ASNs and one ASN may span multiple cities. The registered organization, routing operator and end user are not always the same entity; an organization name does not identify a device or person.
ip.faq.missingFields: Why are risk scores or some fields missing?
ip.faq.missingFieldsAnswer: Only information actually returned by sources is displayed. A missing risk score, coordinates or proxy flag does not mean the IP is safe or risky. Scores and VPN/proxy labels reflect a particular source's assessment and are not a standalone security conclusion. Fields may be absent because a source omitted them, a query failed or a service is not configured. Do not read “unknown” as “no” or zero risk.
ip.faq.findEgress: How do I find my network's egress IP?
ip.faq.findEgressAnswer: The home page's IPv4 and IPv6 cards detect egress through your browser. Click an address for detailed location information. With a proxy or split routing, different sites may use different egress addresses. Use the home page's website routing results to choose the address to inspect.
ip.faq.lookupHistory: Where are recent lookups stored and how are they updated?
ip.faq.lookupHistoryAnswer: This browser keeps the last 10 successful lookups and their results. Clicking history reads the cached result; click “Look up” again to update. History is stored in localStorage in this browser and does not sync between devices. Clearing site data removes it. Queried addresses may also appear in the address bar and browser history.
